Once a thriving moon clustered with many cities, Trite was the place to be. However deep into the war there was a catastrophic attack, leaving the cities in ash. Many had fled and left their stuff behind. But it is still riddled with remants of war.

> Weather

Trite can experience Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane, or Minefield weather by default.

> Moon Exclusive Content

Inside & Outside Ambience

On Trite you can hear two ambiences. One plays inside while the other one plays outside.

Outside Ambience

Inside Ambience

Turrets and Scanners

Trite's exterior has 57 turrets that spawn immediately in set locations. A turret in an alley connected to a path directly behind the ship is immediately active upon landing.

The rest of these turrets are activated by triggering a Scanner. This is a map hazard attached to metal poles on the exterior. When a player walks near one or at a specific position near one, it will drop down and turn on a red search light that patrols the area in a back-and-forth motion. Any player that walks into this search light will make the light turn green and activate several nearby turrets for the rest of the day.

Lone Listeners

Trite's interior has a unique map hazard called a Lone listener. They can be heard constantly playing music throughout the day to indicate their position. When a player is alone and approaches a listener, it will play a voiceline, play its music at a lower pitch, turn on its light, and begin tracking the player for about 10 seconds. If the player makes any noise during this time, such as talking, walking, etc., the listener will attempt to flash the player with its light and rapidly deal 999 damage per hit. This flash can be obstructed with walls, can be triggered through walls, and makes the listener inactive for the rest of the day. If the player does not make noise during this time, the listener will go back to playing its normal music and repeat the process when another lone player gets close to it.

Skyscraper's Fire Exit

Trite has a lone interior fire exit that leads to the top of the right skyscraper. It is technically possible to get to this fire exit with a jetpack from the exterior, but it is ill-advised to attempt doing so. Dropping items at this high of an altitude will suspend them in the air, so this fire exit should be primarily used as a last resort for escaping. Players can use a Health-stim to overcap their hp and survive the fall from the top of the skyscraper. Walking or jumping straight off from the edge of the fire exit will have the player end up nearby if not directly on the ship.

Falling Building

To the north and slightly east of the ship is a building that can either randomly fall or can be triggered to fall by a player that interacts with it for about 120 seconds. Either way, the building will begin to fall forward into another building and cause a domino effect of moving several buildings. After about 60 seconds the building south of the ship will begin to move and crash onto the ground next to the ship if the building randomly started falling or almost onto the ship itself if a player triggered the fall, dealing 200 damage to any player underneath it. The ship will take off and return to orbit to avoid being crushed by the building if a player triggered the fall.

Major Story Spoilers: Decision or Failure Aftermath

If players decided to not overload and blow up ResearcherxB or otherwise did not successfully locate the ship, players will receive a distress signal that tells them their time is up and that ResearcherxB will crash onto Trite. ResearcherxB will become inaccessible on that save file past this point. The next time players land on Trite, they will receive a signal, usually in the afternoon, that the ship is about to crash. The ship will then crash onto Trite's exterior in roughly another hour of in-game time.

If players land on Trite in the future on that save file, it will have been completely overrun by white mold. Several Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior immediately upon landing and large portions of the interior will be covered in growth, obscuring vision.

> Lore

Trite was a thriving and powerful moon in the region under the rule of the Emperor. However, the Triton military's destruction of Calist was the catalyst for a war that eventually lead to Trite being bombarded and decimated by opposing dominions.

Radio Message 3

Radio message 3 continues the story of the Across the Stars radio host, unlocking Filitrios when logged. They cover the fall of Trite and recommed to head to Demetrica.

Text ⁠
This is
-Across The Stars-
Back with the 11-ish AM news, I’m a little late today.
There’s a lot to catch up on nowadays.
It’s been a cloudy week and it looks like it’ll be cloudy for a little while longer.

The reports have not been great.. quite the opposite in fact.
If you haven’t heard it already, Trite has suffered its most devastating attack yet.
..The cities have fallen.
I’ll repeat it once more, the cities of Trite have fallen.
According to my sources most of the people were able to flee in time.
I wish I could say I know what will happen next.
But..
I can’t.
What the Triton Military will do next is a mystery.

All I can say is go to the Domes of Demetrica, and survive.

There will be some comforting tunes, please, stay tuned.
And for those still listening, thank you.

Children's Drawings

Children's drawings depict a family living on Trite during the war. After an argument over heading to the domes on Demetrica, one of the parents gets killed by a Coil-Head. The remaining parent and child then leave their now ruined home and attempt to find salvation on Demetrica. These randomly spawn as scrap within the interior and can not be logged.
